headline_marked: India women [[refuse Asia Cup trophy from Naqvi]] after 8th title win
headline: India women refuse Asia Cup trophy from Naqvi after 8th title win
summary: The Harmanpreet Kaur-led side declined to accept the trophy from ACC president Mohsin Naqvi in Dubai, mirroring a similar stand by the men's team last year.
details: India's women's cricket team won their eighth Women's Asia Cup title after defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final in Dubai.
Despite the victory, the team refused to receive the trophy or tournament medals from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi during the post-match presentation.
Naqvi, who also serves as the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and Pakistan's interior minister, was present at the ceremony, which was delayed by nearly 50 minutes.
The incident follows a similar pattern from last year's men's Asia Cup final, where the Indian men's team also declined to accept the trophy from Naqvi.
Instead of the official ceremony, the Indian team held its own brief presentation where BCCI officials handed out medals, including the best-fielder award to Nandani Sharma.
The decision is attributed to strained cricketing relations between India and Pakistan following heightened cross-border tensions in May 2025.
Head coach Amol Muzumdar stated that the team fully supports the BCCI's position, emphasizing that being champions is what matters most to the unit.
caption:
Champions but no trophy? India's women's team refuses to accept the Asia Cup prize from Mohsin Naqvi.

India's women's cricket team won their eighth Women's Asia Cup title after defeating Sri Lanka by 72 runs in the final in Dubai.

Despite the victory, the team refused to receive the trophy or tournament medals from Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi during the post-match presentation.

Naqvi, who also serves as the chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board and Pakistan's interior minister, was present at the ceremony, which was delayed by nearly 50 minutes.

The incident follows a similar pattern from last year's men's Asia Cup final, where the Indian men's team also declined to accept the trophy from Naqvi.

Instead of the official ceremony, the Indian team held its own brief presentation where BCCI officials handed out medals, including the best-fielder award to Nandani Sharma.

The decision is attributed to strained cricketing relations between India and Pakistan following heightened cross-border tensions in May 2025.

Head coach Amol Muzumdar stated that the team fully supports the BCCI's position, emphasizing that being champions is what matters most to the unit.

headline_marked: Trump [[dismisses report China helped Iran]] before attack on US base
headline: Trump dismisses report China helped Iran before attack on US base
summary: The US President brushed aside claims that Chinese entities provided satellite imagery of a Jordan base to Iran before an attack that killed three US troops.
details: US President Donald Trump dismissed a report suggesting that Chinese entities helped Iran acquire satellite images of a US base in Jordan before an attack in July that killed three US troops.

The claim, originally reported by the Wall Street Journal, cited unnamed US officials who stated that imagery was provided to Iran, though they did not allege direct involvement by the Chinese government in Beijing.

When asked if he would raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping during an upcoming meeting, Trump did not answer directly, instead stating that both the US and China engage in similar surveillance activities.
Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that while China spies on the US, the US also spies on China, essentially equating the surveillance practices of both nations.
The two presidents are expected to meet in the United States on September 24, although China has not yet officially confirmed the meeting.
Trump reiterated that he maintains a good relationship with President Xi, describing their behavior toward each other as reasonably well.
The administration's stance appears to be an effort to downplay tensions between Washington and Beijing despite ongoing frustrations over China's close ties with Tehran.
caption:
Did China help Iran attack a US base? President Trump says 'they basically do what we do' regarding spying.

US President Donald Trump dismissed a report suggesting that Chinese entities helped Iran acquire satellite images of a US base in Jordan before an attack in July that killed three US troops.

The claim, originally reported by the Wall Street Journal, cited unnamed US officials who stated that imagery was provided to Iran, though they did not allege direct involvement by the Chinese government in Beijing.

When asked if he would raise the issue with Chinese President Xi Jinping during an upcoming meeting, Trump did not answer directly, instead stating that both the US and China engage in similar surveillance activities.

Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that while China spies on the US, the US also spies on China, essentially equating the surveillance practices of both nations.

The two presidents are expected to meet in the United States on September 24, although China has not yet officially confirmed the meeting.

Trump reiterated that he maintains a good relationship with President Xi, describing their behavior toward each other as reasonably well.

The administration's stance appears to be an effort to downplay tensions between Washington and Beijing despite ongoing frustrations over China's close ties with Tehran.
